title: HTTP /deployments/health/read serves environment state, the last error line and the open incident, composed into the production listener
description:
PREREQUISITE row filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 while planning task-85895a88a2484d8589046b2030efd445 (the Needs-you incident card), which cannot read anything without it. Grandchild A task-df972c274f2a4 (the Environments surface, order 123.1) needs the SAME read, so this row serves both and is filed once rather than twice.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04):
- `ls apps/daemon/src/http/ | grep -i incident` returns NOTHING. No deployment-health or incident route exists.
- `/health/read` EXISTS and is NOT this. apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts (217 lines) is mounted (daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:51) and proxy-pinned (dev-proxy-paths.ts:24), but its `HealthView` (:51) covers PROVIDER PAUSE and REPOSITORY RESERVATION - the DAEMON's own health. It is not deployment environment health and the two must not be conflated: overloading it would make one route mean two unrelated things and would put an environment outage behind a daemon-liveness code.
- The durable incident and the probe ring are task-6ec875f4dd5f4f2ab97e46f71bf57b2b's (order 121, its grandchild B task-cc05c473 writes `moe-health-probe/1`, the bounded 1440 ring, the derived UP/DEGRADED/DOWN and the one-open-incident lifecycle). That row is explicitly forbidden from touching any UI, and it writes a DURABLE RECORD with no HTTP surface. This row is the operator-facing read over it.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `/deployments/health/read` serving, per environment, the DERIVED state (UP / DEGRADED / DOWN), the last probe with its timestamp and latency, THE LAST ERROR LINE VERBATIM, the open incident if any with when it opened, and the PREVIOUS DEPLOY RECEIPT's sha so a consumer can name a rollback target - plus its composition into the PRODUCTION listener, in the SAME row.

DO NOT REPEAT THE DESIGN-READ SPLIT: task-7ca9dca3 served /design/read and task-eb2bb09d then had to exist purely to compose the port into the listener, because a served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. The pattern to follow is apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts with its .js bridge and test, composed through http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts, http-listener-guards.ts and daemon-entry.ts.

THE LAST ERROR LINE IS THE POINT. The consuming card's whole reason for existing is that an operator under time pressure should not have to open the logs; a read that returns "unhealthy" instead of the actual error line makes that card useless. Carry the probe's recorded error text verbatim.

THE STATE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED (that row's rail 4). This read RE-DERIVES from the ring or calls that row's derivation; it must not add a stored status field, which would become a second source of truth that can disagree with its own history.
definitionOfDone: `/deployments/health/read` serves, per environment: the derived state (UP / DEGRADED / DOWN), the last probe (timestamp and latencyMs), THE LAST ERROR LINE VERBATIM, the open incident with its opened-at when one exists, and the previous deploy receipt's sha. Built from the EXISTING probe ring and incident records - it reimplements no derivation and adds NO stored status field. Assert the reuse with a grep in the completion record.

THE LAST ERROR LINE IS VERBATIM, asserted as its own arm: seed a probe failure with a distinctive error text and assert that exact string is what the route returns - not a summary, not a truncation, not a code. A read that returns 'unhealthy' makes the incident card it feeds useless, which is the whole reason this route exists.

THE ROUTE IS COMPOSED INTO THE PRODUCTION LISTENER IN THIS SAME ROW - http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts / http-listener-guards.ts and daemon-entry.ts, following the design-read precedent. Assert it is reachable from the COMPOSED production listener, not only from a hand-built test server: a served route nothing mounts is exactly why task-eb2bb09d had to exist after task-7ca9dca3.

AN ENVIRONMENT THAT CANNOT BE PROBED IS NEVER REPORTED UP - it carries the probe row's PROBE_URL_MISSING outcome with its code AND layer. Assert the state is not UP, not merely that a refusal member is present.
The response decoder contract is EXACT-KEY: an unknown key and a missing key each refuse with the specific code AND the layer that refused, never merely that decoding failed.

It is DISTINCT from /health/read and does not touch it: apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts serves daemon provider-pause and repository-reservation state, and `git status --porcelain` proves that file is untouched. Two unrelated meanings behind one route is a rejection.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: SERVE AND COMPOSE IN THE SAME ROW. A route that is served but not mounted is the failure that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
THE LAST ERROR LINE IS CARRIED VERBATIM. Summarising it defeats the card this read exists to feed.
THE STATE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED. Re-derive from the ring or call the probe row's derivation; a stored status field is a second source of truth that can disagree with its own history.
DO NOT OVERLOAD /health/read. It serves the DAEMON's health (provider pause, repository reservation), not deployment environments. Leave apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts untouched.

NO UI, NO PROXY PIN, NO CLIENT DECODER: the control-room half belongs to task-85895a88a2484d8589046b2030efd445 and task-df972c274f2a4, and touching apps/control-room here collides in the shared worktree.
Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE THE RECORDS YOU READ BEFORE NAMING A FIELD. This route serves facts written by task-6ec875f4's grandchild task-cc05c47362dc41b0b2b416a70ad45b42 — `moe-health-probe/1`, the bounded 1440 ring, the derived UP/DEGRADED/DOWN and the one-open-incident lifecycle. That row was unlanded at plan time, so this plan names none of its fields. Your dependsOn gates the WORKING claim until it lands.

Run and read the OUTPUT:
  (a) `grep -rn 'moe-health-probe' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts` — must return the record writer. If empty, `moe.report_blocked` with blockedOnTaskIds ["task-6ec875f4dd5f4f2ab97e46f71bf57b2b"] and stop; inventing a record shape here produces a route that decodes nothing and serves plausible blanks.
  (b) Read that row's completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings and RECORD: the exact probe record fields, the name of its DERIVATION function, and the incident record's shape including its opened-at.
  (c) `grep -rn 'deploy-receipt\|DeployReceipt' apps packages --include=*.ts` — DoD 1 wants the PREVIOUS deploy receipt's sha as a rollback target. That receipt is task-04b3ce7e's and was unlanded when the sibling rows were filed. If it is still absent, serve the field as explicitly absent and SAY SO in the record — do not invent a receipt shape, because the sibling rollback work resolves through the same receipts.

CALL THE EXISTING DERIVATION, DO NOT REIMPLEMENT IT (rail 3). DoD 1 asks you to prove reuse with a grep in the completion record. A second derivation of UP/DEGRADED/DOWN over the same ring is a second opinion that will eventually disagree with the first, and the browser will show whichever this route returns.

THE ROUTE MODULE — new `apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./deployments-health-read.ts";`, exactly as `design-read.js` does).

COPY apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts (102 lines) STRUCTURALLY — it is the precedent this row's description names, and its shape answers most of the DoD:
  - `export const DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_READ_PATH = "/deployments/health/read" as const;` (design-read.ts:13)
  - `const LAYER = "…" as const;` MODULE-LOCAL (design-read.ts:14). READ RAIL 6 CAREFULLY: it forbids introducing a new exported `*_LAYER` CONSTANT, because an exported layer constant is enumerated by the boundary roster and demands a four-file coupled backfill this row does not own. A module-local `const LAYER` is exactly what the precedent does and is NOT that — do not read rail 6 as forbidding a layer altogether, because DoD 4 and 5 both require one.
  - A frozen CLOSED code roster, like `DESIGN_READ_CODES` (:16).
  - A `refused(code, layer = LAYER)` factory (:29) so no call site can pair a code with the wrong layer.
  - A PORT INTERFACE the module does not construct — `DesignReadPort` (:25) is documented as "Closed over a store by tests and by the composition sibling; this module does not open one." Yours takes the probe/incident reads the same way. This is what lets step 4 mount it and the tests inject it.
  - EXACT-KEY BODY DECODING via `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` then an explicit allowed-keys check (:38-57). Note the header rule at :1-5: `projectId` comes from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL, and a payload that names it is an UNKNOWN KEY, not a convenience. Keep that.

SERVE, per environment: derived state, last probe (timestamp + latencyMs), THE LAST ERROR LINE VERBATIM, the open incident with its opened-at when one exists, and the previous deploy receipt's sha. ADD NO STORED STATUS FIELD (rail 3).

Keep it near design-read's size. If it runs long, the shape is wrong — this module decodes, delegates and projects; it computes nothing.

RED TESTS FOR THE ROUTE, before composing it.

  1. THE VERBATIM ERROR LINE (DoD 2), and it is this row's reason for existing. Seed a probe failure whose error text is a DISTINCTIVE literal — something no summariser would produce, with punctuation and length — and assert the route returns that EXACT string. Not a substring match, not "contains an error", not a code. Assert equality. The card this feeds exists so an operator under time pressure does not open the logs; a route returning "unhealthy" makes it useless while looking correct.
  2. AN UNPROBEABLE ENVIRONMENT IS NEVER UP (DoD 4). An environment with a deploy receipt but no health URL carries the probe row's PROBE_URL_MISSING outcome with its code AND its layer, and the STATE IS NOT UP. Assert the state — asserting only that a refusal member is present passes for a response that reports UP with a refusal hanging off it.
  3. EXACT-KEY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (DoD 5): an UNKNOWN key refuses, and a MISSING key refuses, each with the specific code AND the layer that refused. "Decoding failed" is not the assertion — a single generic code for both makes the two indistinguishable to a client.
  4. `projectId` IN THE PAYLOAD IS AN UNKNOWN KEY, not an override. The principal is the authority; assert the refusal rather than assuming it.
  5. THE STATE COMES FROM THE EXISTING DERIVATION (DoD 1). Feed a ring whose derived state would differ from any naive rule over the same latencies, and assert the route returns the DERIVATION's answer. A fixture where both agree proves nothing about which one ran.
  6. NO OPEN INCIDENT is a normal, healthy answer — the incident member is explicitly absent rather than a fabricated empty object.

COMPOSE IT INTO THE PRODUCTION LISTENER — IN THIS ROW (rail 1, DoD 3). This is the step the row exists to prevent skipping: task-7ca9dca3 served `/design/read` and task-eb2bb09d then had to exist PURELY to mount it, because a served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

FOUR EDITS, each traced from the design-read precedent at HEAD:
  1. `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` — import the path and handler beside the design import at :36, and pass the port through where :368 passes `designReads`.
  2. `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts` — `import type { …Port }` beside :20, and add the OPTIONAL port to the options interface beside :157-158. Copy that field's comment convention: "Absent means the design-revision read refuses as unavailable" — an absent port must make the read REFUSE as unavailable, never throw and never answer a healthy default.
  3. `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-guards.ts` — the transport-pair guard beside :91 ("The design-revision read: same transport pair").
  4. `apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts` — the conditional spread at :288: `...(resolved.X === undefined ? {} : { X: resolved.X })`.

TWO OF THESE FILES ARE ALREADY OVER THE 400-LINE CAP — measured: read-dispatch is 557 and guards is 411 (listener 352, daemon-entry 334). That is PRE-EXISTING and NOT this row's to fix. Add the fewest lines the wiring needs, and NOTE the pre-existing sizes in your step note so a reviewer does not attribute them to you. Do NOT attempt a split: it would be a large out-of-scope refactor in files several rows are moving through.

DoD 3 REQUIRES REACHABILITY FROM THE COMPOSED PRODUCTION LISTENER, not from a hand-built test server. Assert against the listener the production entry actually builds — a test that constructs its own server and mounts your handler proves the handler works and proves nothing about whether the daemon serves it, which is precisely the hole that forced the earlier split.

GATES AND DRILLS.

GATES, each STANDALONE and FOREGROUND — no pipe, no `;` chain, no `&&` (a piped run reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
  2. `pnpm typecheck`
READ THE OUTPUT, NOT THE EXIT CODE: a missed `--filter` exits 0, and "No test files found" / "0 passed" are also exit 0. The discriminator is `Test Files N passed` with N nonzero — quote it for both. DoD 7 is explicit: root `pnpm test` covers NO `apps/**` file, so SAY that rather than quoting a bare root count line. Name `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` as the complete_task verification command.

The daemon suite is slow (~22 min) and flaky on this branch (two back-to-back baselines gave `17 failed | 416 passed` then `10 failed | 423 passed`, dominated by 30000ms timeouts), so attribute red by PATH per global rail 3. Run your own suite and the listener suites targeted first.

DRILL 1, THE COMPOSITION. Remove the `daemon-entry.ts` wiring only. The DoD-3 reachability arm MUST go red. If it stays green, that arm is hitting a hand-built server rather than the composed production listener — rewrite it, because as written it would have passed for the exact defect that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist.
DRILL 2, THE ERROR LINE. Make the route return a summary instead of the recorded text. The verbatim arm must go red. If it only checks that the field is non-empty, strengthen it to equality.
DRILL 3, THE ABSENT PORT. Build the listener with the port undefined. The read must REFUSE AS UNAVAILABLE with its code and layer — not throw, and not answer a healthy default. An absent port answering UP would report every environment healthy on a daemon that cannot see any of them.

RESTORE PROOF, global rail 13. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths BEFORE drilling. The four composition files are TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is valid proof, run in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Your new route module, its bridge and its test are UNTRACKED and `git diff` is BLIND to them — back each up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) before mutating and prove the restore by SHA256 equality against that backup.

COMPLETION RECORD states: `git status --porcelain` proving `apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts` is UNTOUCHED (DoD 6 — it serves the DAEMON's provider-pause and repository-reservation state, a different meaning that must not share this route); the grep proving the derivation is REUSED and no stored status field was added (DoD 1); the four composition edits by file and line; the pre-existing 557/411 line counts you did not create; whether the deploy-receipt sha was servable or explicitly absent; and the three drill outcomes with restore proofs.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SERVING WITHOUT COMPOSING — the failure this row exists to prevent, and it has a named precedent on this board: task-7ca9dca3 served /design/read and task-eb2bb09d had to exist purely to mount it. Hence composition in the same row, and hence DoD 3's insistence on reachability from the COMPOSED production listener rather than a hand-built test server. Drill 1 (remove the daemon-entry wiring) is what proves the arm is the right kind — an arm hitting its own server would have passed for the original defect.

OVERLOADING /health/read — rejected by rail 4 and by meaning: health-read.ts (217 lines) serves the DAEMON's provider-pause and repository-reservation state. Putting deployment-environment health behind the same route would make one path mean two unrelated things and would put an environment outage behind a daemon-liveness code. DoD 6 wants `git status --porcelain` proving that file untouched.

RE-DERIVING THE STATE IN THIS ROUTE — rejected by rail 3. A second derivation over the same ring is a second opinion that will eventually disagree, and this route's answer is the one the browser renders. Test 5 uses a ring where the derivation and a naive rule DIVERGE, because a fixture where they agree cannot tell which one ran.

SPLITTING THE OVERSIZED COMPOSITION FILES — rejected as out of scope: 557 and 411 lines are pre-existing, the files are contended, and a refactor there would dwarf this row.

INVENTING THE DEPLOY-RECEIPT SHAPE for the rollback-target sha — rejected. It is a sibling parent's row and the rollback work resolves through the same receipts; serving the field as explicitly absent and recording that is honest, while a guessed shape would diverge silently.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by architect-aa54e231 on branch moe/work-2026-09-04. The row was filed by architect-fa3a3e17 and its measurements hold; I verified the composition chain and the template it names, and found two things worth adding.

THE COMPOSITION CHAIN IS EXACTLY FOUR EDITS, traced from the design-read precedent:
  http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:36 (import path + handler) and :368 (pass the port through)
  http-listener.ts:20 (`import type { DesignReadPort }`) and :157-158 (OPTIONAL port on the options interface, with the comment "Absent means the design-revision read refuses as unavailable")
  http-listener-guards.ts:91 ("The design-revision read: same transport pair")
  daemon-entry.ts:288 (`...(resolved.designReads === undefined ? {} : { designReads: resolved.designReads })`)

TWO OF THOSE FILES ARE ALREADY PAST THE 400-LINE HARD CAP: http-listener-read-dispatch.ts is 557 and http-listener-guards.ts is 411 (http-listener.ts 352, daemon-entry.ts 334). PRE-EXISTING, not this row's to fix, and splitting them would be a large out-of-scope refactor in files several rows move through. The plan tells the worker to add the fewest lines the wiring needs and to NOTE the counts so a reviewer does not attribute them to this diff.

RAIL 6 IS AMBIGUOUS AND THE PRECEDENT RESOLVES IT. The rail says "reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant". design-read.ts:14 declares `const LAYER = "DESIGN_READ" as const` — MODULE-LOCAL, not exported. So what the rail forbids is an EXPORTED `*_LAYER` constant, which the boundary roster enumerates and which demands a four-file coupled backfill; a module-local `const LAYER` is what the precedent does and is fine. Read literally, the rail could be taken as forbidding a layer at all, which would contradict DoD 4 and DoD 5 — both require a layer. The plan says this explicitly so the worker does not resolve the contradiction the wrong way or stop to ask.

THE TEMPLATE, apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts (102 lines), answers most of the DoD structurally: a `*_PATH` const (:13), the module-local LAYER (:14), a frozen closed code roster (:16), a `refused(code, layer = LAYER)` factory (:29) so no call site can mispair code and layer, a PORT interface the module does not construct (:25, documented as "Closed over a store by tests and by the composition sibling; this module does not open one"), and exact-key body decoding via `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` plus an explicit allowed-keys check (:38-57). Its header (:1-5) states the rule the plan carries forward: projectId comes from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL and a payload naming it is an UNKNOWN KEY. The `.js` bridge is one line: `export * from "./design-read.ts";`.

UPSTREAM RECORDS ARE UNLANDED, so the plan names none of their fields: the probe ring, the derivation and the incident lifecycle belong to task-cc05c473 (under task-6ec875f4, this row's dependsOn), and the deploy receipt belongs to task-04b3ce7e under a sibling parent. Step 1 hard-stops on the former and requires the latter to be served as explicitly absent rather than invented.

THIS ROUTE IS THE MISSING PRODUCER FOR TWO ROWS I PLANNED EARLIER TODAY: task-df972c27 (Environments surface) and task-85895a88 (incident card) both consume it, and both were planned to MEASURE the frame at claim rather than name its fields — which is consistent with this row defining it. Rail 5's "no proxy pin, no client decoder" is complementary rather than conflicting: I placed the DEV_PROXY_PATHS entry and the exact-key decoder in the control-room row that owns them.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A SERVED-BUT-UNMOUNTED ROUTE. The exact defect that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3, and it satisfies every existence grep. The tell is a test that builds its own server: it proves the handler works and says nothing about whether the daemon serves it. Drill 1 catches it by removing the daemon-entry wiring.

2. AN ABSENT PORT ANSWERING HEALTHY. The optional-port pattern means a daemon composed without this port must REFUSE AS UNAVAILABLE. If it instead answers a default, every environment reads UP on a daemon that cannot see any of them — the most dangerous possible output from a health route. Drill 3 targets it.

3. THE ERROR LINE SUMMARISED. This route exists so an operator does not open the logs; returning "unhealthy" makes the consuming card useless while the route looks correct. The arm must assert EQUALITY against a distinctive literal, not a substring or non-emptiness.

4. AN UNPROBEABLE ENVIRONMENT REPORTED UP. Asserting only that a refusal member is present passes for a response that says UP with a refusal hanging off it. DoD 4 wants the STATE asserted.

5. RAIL 6 MISREAD AS FORBIDDING A LAYER. It forbids an exported `*_LAYER` constant (a boundary-roster backfill); the precedent uses a module-local `const LAYER`. Read the other way it contradicts DoD 4 and 5 and would stall the row.

6. REIMPLEMENTED DERIVATION. Two opinions about one ring; the browser shows this route's. A fixture where the derivation and a naive rule agree cannot detect it.

7. THE OVERSIZED COMPOSITION FILES being blamed on this diff, or worse, split by it. 557 and 411 are pre-existing; the plan requires noting them and forbids the refactor.

8. UPSTREAM SHAPES INVENTED. The probe/incident records and the deploy receipt are other rows'. Step 1 hard-stops on the first and requires explicit absence for the second.
